rationale: In the index discovery cohort reported by Schnabel et al. (2023), 100% (5/5) of affected individuals across three unrelated families with homozygous truncating FILIP1 variants presented with microcephaly alongside severe arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, scoliosis, and dysmorphic facies. Subsequent studies (e.g., Chaurasia et al., 2026) corroborate microcephaly as a core hallmark of FILIP1 loss-of-function syndromic arthrogryposis, differentiating it from pure non-syndromic congenital myopathies that lack cranial and central nervous system involvement.

evidence.text: Schnabel et al. reported five affected individuals from three independent consanguineous families with homozygous truncating variants in FILIP1 who all presented with an overlapping clinical phenotype featuring congenital joint contractures, reduced skin creases, microcephaly, and facial dysmorphism.

source.title: Homozygous loss-of-function variants in FILIP1 cause autosomal recessive arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with microcephaly
source.quote: Here, we report five affected individuals from three independent families sharing an overlapping phenotype with congenital contractures affecting shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee and foot as well as scoliosis, reduced palmar and plantar skin folds, microcephaly and facial dysmorphism. Using exome sequencing, we identified homozygous truncating variants in FILIP1 in all patients.

evidence.text: Chaurasia et al. evaluated rare homozygous copy number losses and validated FILIP1 biallelic variants as causing syndromic arthrogryposis accompanied by microcephaly.

source.title: Systematic analysis of homozygous autosomal copy number losses in exomes improves diagnostic yield and uncovers ultra-rare recessive disorders
source.quote: Further analysis of the data and identification of additional affected individuals through collaboration led to identification of biallelic FILIP1 and FAM177A1 variants as causes of a syndromic arthrogryposis and a neuromuscular disorder respectively.

new_directions.question_text: Does the severity or onset of microcephaly (congenital primary vs. secondary progressive postnatal microcephaly) vary across different biallelic FILIP1 variant types?
new_directions.rationale: Tracking head circumference percentiles longitudinally across larger cohorts will determine whether cranial growth failure is already present at birth or progressive postnatally.

new_directions.question_text: To what extent can neuroimaging findings (e.g., cortical migration defects or simplified gyral patterns) distinguish FILIP1-related arthrogryposis from other syndromic forms of arthrogryposis multiplex congenita?
new_directions.rationale: Because FILIP1 regulates filamin degradation and radial cortical migration, structural CNS anomalies may be an essential discriminator alongside head circumference.
